tier_reason: Third-party Wuffs doc/benchmarks.md (PNG section) lists mimiclodepng rows against mimiclibpng = 1.00x with public harness code (test/c/std/png.c plus test/c/mimiclib/png.c, lodepng branch), -O3 recipe in the png.c header comment, compilers clang 11.0.1 / gcc 10.2.1, and CPU Intel Core i5-10210U; same page and tier as the wave 10 libspng retier to A.

corrections.compiler_and_flags: clang 11.0.1 and gcc 10.2.1 are the Debian Bullseye compilers named on the page (it does not say which one built the mimic rows, which carry no compiler suffix); recipe in the header comment of test/c/std/png.c is -O3 plus the 'wuffs mimic cflags' -DWUFFS_MIMIC -lm -lpng -lz. To bench lodepng instead of libpng, test/c/mimiclib/png.c must be edited: the line '#define WUFFS_MIMICLIB_USE_LODEPNG_INSTEAD_OF_LIBPNG 1' ships commented out and the '#include "/path/to/your/copy/of/github.com/lvandeve/lodepng/lodepng.cpp"' placeholder path must point at a lodepng checkout (20220717 in the table). libpng 1.6.37 and zlib 1.2.11 are the Debian Bullseye system builds.
corrections.caveats: The project itself makes no speed claim (README has no performance section); the numbers come from the Wuffs project's mimic benchmark. Mixed result: lodepng is 1.09-1.13x faster than libpng only on the three small images (19k, 40k, 77k decoded bytes) and slower on the two larger ones (0.89x on 552k_32bpp_verify_checksum, 0.77x on 4002k_24bpp); geometric mean over the five rows is about 0.99x (derived from page data), i.e. parity overall. On the same page libspng (1.02-1.60x) and stb_image (0.76-1.23x) are comparable or better alternatives, and Wuffs itself is 1.55-3.16x. Decode only; no encode numbers against libpng were reached (fpng's README and lodepng issue #179 show lodepng encoding at ~3-17 MP/s with no libpng row). The libpng baseline is the Debian system build linked to zlib 1.2.11, whose inflate is slow; a libpng built on zlib-ng or libdeflate would likely widen lodepng's deficit on large images. The harness slightly handicaps lodepng: lodepng_decode_memory allocates its own output buffer that the mimic code then memcpy's into Wuffs' dst (plus a per-pixel RGBA-to-BGRA swap on the 32bpp image), while the libpng simplified-API path decodes straight into dst. lodepng version in the table is 20220717, older than the current repo (numbers measured September 2022). The page does not state which of clang/gcc built the mimic rows, and the lodepng mimic path does not support the ignore-checksum quirk, so only the verify_checksum row exists for the 552k image.

notes: All five lodepng numbers and vs_mimic ratios match the PNG table of google/wuffs doc/benchmarks.md exactly; metadata verified (Zlib license, 2.3k stars, not a fork or archived, last commit 2026-10-06, active). Shortcomings to record: only a partial win (faster on small images, 0.77-0.89x on large ones, ~0.99x geomean derived from page data), third-party 2022 numbers on lodepng 20220717 against a zlib-1.2.11-based libpng, no encode comparison, and libspng/stb/Wuffs are faster alternatives on the same page.
